## Concurrency and deployment evidence only

| Slot | SQLite WAL | PostgreSQL |
|---|---|---|
| Reader/writer interaction | WAL: “readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers.” | MVCC: “reading never blocks writing and writing never blocks reading.” Explicit table/row locking exists, so do not generalize this guarantee to deliberately locked workflows. |
| Concurrent-writer conflict | SQLite serializes writes: “There can only be a single writer at a time”; connections that write “have to take turns.” | A conflicting updater waits for the first updater to commit or roll back. At Repeatable Read/Serializable, applications must be prepared to retry serialization failures. |
| Local vs network deployment | WAL requires all database-using processes on one host and “does not work over a network filesystem.” | The server can listen for client connections on configured TCP/IP addresses; an empty address list means Unix-domain sockets only. Network exposure is configurable. |

### Decisive official passages

- **SQLite, writer serialization:** [Isolation In SQLite](https://www.sqlite.org/isolation.html)  
  “SQLite implements serializable transactions by actually serializing the writes. **There can only be a single writer at a time** … [writers] **have to take turns**.”

- **SQLite WAL reader/writer and host constraint:** [Write-Ahead Logging](https://www.sqlite.org/wal.html)  
  “WAL provides more concurrency as **readers do not block writers and a writer does not block readers**.”  
  “**All processes using a database must be on the same host computer; WAL does not work over a network filesystem.**”

- **PostgreSQL reader/writer:** [PostgreSQL current, MVCC introduction](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/mvcc-intro.html)  
  “reading never blocks writing and writing never blocks reading.”

- **PostgreSQL writer conflicts:** [PostgreSQL current, Transaction Isolation](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/transaction-iso.html)  
  “the would-be updater **will wait for the first updating transaction to commit or roll back**.”  
  “Applications using [Repeatable Read/Serializable] must be prepared to retry transactions due to **serialization failures**.”

- **PostgreSQL deployment:** [PostgreSQL current, Connection Settings](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/runtime-config-connection.html)  
  `listen_addresses` “specifies the TCP/IP address(es) on which the server is to listen for connections from client applications.”

### Applicability, contradictions, gaps

- SQLite WAL is documented as available since **SQLite 3.7.0 (2010-07-21)**. PostgreSQL URLs use `/current/`; retrieved passages did not pin a release number.
- No contradiction: SQLite WAL permits reader/writer overlap while still permitting only one writer.
- Configuration-dependent gap: the service’s PostgreSQL transaction isolation level and use of explicit locking are unspecified. No online-backup findings were collected.
